chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bought goods, so the goods became unsalable upon him, and he had already paid the zakat of his wealth before purchasing them with it. Is there zakat upon him, or (does he wait) until he sells it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he withheld it in order to seek the profit (price rise) upon the capital, then upon him is the zakat.'

key_terms.كَسَدَ: To become unsalable or stagnant in the market

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of zakat on trade goods that become unsalable if the owner held them for price speculation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that zakat is due on trade goods if they were held with the intent of speculation (iltimās al-faḍl), even if they become unsalable (kasād) before sale. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between mere holding and active commercial intent, linking the obligation to the owner's purpose rather than just the state of the goods. This ruling underscores the principle that zakat on merchandise is triggered by the intention to profit from market fluctuations, a key concept in Islamic commercial jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Abu Al Rabih Al Shamu, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding a man who buys goods, so the goods become unsalable upon him, and he had already purified (paid Zakāt of) his wealth before having purchased it. Is there Zakāt upon him, or until (after) he sells it?’ So heasws said: ‘If he withheld it in order to seek the extra upon the capital wealth (from the price rise), so upon him is the Zakāt’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from abu Rabi‘ al- Shamiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who purchases a certain kind of goods but its value falls. He had paid Zakat before purchasing such asset. Is there Zakat on him or Zakat becomes due when he sells it? He (the Imam) said, ’If he had held it to increase his capital, he is required to pay Zakat.’”
